## Rule

ARC-GEN `task_5614dbcf`: the input is a 9x9 canvas interpreted as a 3x3 grid of 3x3 cells. Occupied cells are solid non-gray colors, with up to two gray noise pixels inserted in any cell. Empty cells can also contain gray noise. The output is the 3x3 color map: occupied cells keep their non-gray color, empty/noise-only cells are background.

## Algorithm sketch

For each 3x3 cell, inspect the first row's three pixels. Because the generator can gray out at most two pixels per cell, at least one of those three pixels remains the true non-gray color for every occupied cell. The current best uses one `Einsum('nchw,c,rh,sw->nrs')` to contract the free input with powers-of-four color weights, row selectors for rows 0/3/6, and column selectors for groups 0..2/3..5/6..8. Background and gray both map to 1, so `Floor(Log(sum) / Log(4))` recovers the color id; `Equal(ids)` creates the 3x3 one-hot and opset-18 `Pad` writes the 30x30 bool output.

### Sub-30 / perfect-25 audit — WALL (2026-07-07, bo_ng_cld_worker1)
The prompt's "perfect-25 / cost≤1" rumor is **FALSE**: this is a genuine 9×9→3×3 color-map
reduction with gray-noise suppression, not an identity/geometry task. Three independent
from-scratch formulations all bottom out at 30 (details: `hard_records/perfect25_and_sub30_wall.md`):

| route | params | gate | result |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Identity / Transpose(0,1,3,2) (zero-param family) | 0 | visible | **0/265 FAIL** |
| Conv width-2 (2 taps/cell) | 20 | visible | **253/265 FAIL** (2 gray kill both taps) |
| MaxPool→Mul→Pad (param-free reducer, correct) | 18 | visible **PASS** | **cost 8018** (mem 8000) — 267× worse |

**Forced-floor argument** (memory model = `neurogolf_utils.calculate_memory`):
1. `calculate_memory` charges every node-output tensor its full byte size **except** the two named
   `input`/`output`. ⇒ any 2+ node graph pays ≥1 charged intermediate; the smallest useful one
   (`[1,10,3,3]` INT8 = 90 B, or `[1,10,10,10]` F32 = 4,000 B) already ≫ 30. ⇒ **champion must be a
   single input→output node (memory 0)**.
2. A single param-free op (Identity/Transpose/Slice/Pool) can't both suppress gray per-channel and
   per-cell-reduce; pools are channel-blind, and ONNX pools reject `pad ≥ kernel` so they can't even
   reshape to 30×30 in one node. ⇒ the node must carry per-channel weights ⇒ **Conv**.
3. ≤2 gray anywhere in a cell ⇒ a robust witness needs ≥3 distinct taps (any 2-tap set can be fully
   grayed — 253/265). 3 taps × 10 forced output channels (output contract) = **30**; Conv weight
   dim-0 must equal the 10 output channels (kernel dims uniform, gray channel can't drop to 0 taps).

⇒ **30 = 3 forced taps × 10 forced channels is exact. Sub-30 is impossible under the current cost
model + generator guarantee. No candidate staged (a win requires strictly < 30).**

## Don't-do log

- Do not continue compressing the current LIVE crop9x9 graph first; it materializes `[1,10,9,9]` F32 and is stuck around 5148.
- Do not carry per-color planes after the witness sample if using this rule; scalar color-index plus Equal tail is cheaper.
- Do not sample only one or two pixels per 3x3 cell; the generator can gray out two pixels in one cell.
- Full 3x3 pooling per color is correct but keeps the larger multi-channel crop/pool structure and loses to the 3-pixel witness.
- Do not continue the 772 Conv interval scan first; the reproduced Einsum/logdecode route dominates it at 441.
